message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on a decorative hedgehog figure made of Styrofoam and covered with natural materials. Such items are typically classified as festive/other decorative articles or as artificial/other articles of plant materials.

Candidates:
- 4421.99 (other articles of wood) or 4602 (basketwork) are possible.
- 9505.90 (festive articles) applies only if the item is for a festive occasion, and this hedgehog is not.
- 6702 (artificial flowers, foliage) is not a good fit.
- 4421.99.97 and 4602.19 are less likely.
- 9989 is not applicable.
- 4420.19 (statuettes and other ornaments of wood) is also possible.

The essential character is hard to pin down. The sisal covers 40% of the figure and the remainder is a mix of materials. Sisal is a vegetable material of heading 5303 or 1404, and a figure made of mixed natural vegetable materials could fall under 1404. In practice, a "decorative hedgehog" ruling classified such items in 4420.10 for wooden statuettes or in 4602. I recall rulings that classified figures covered with natural materials as "Other: Of vegetable materials" under 4602.19.

I'm going with 4602.19.2900, which covers other basketwork, wickerwork and other articles made directly to shape from plaiting materials. That is a less certain fit for a Styrofoam form covered with materials.

An alternative is 9505.90.6000, but that heading requires festive use. The better-supported choice is 4420.19, which would be "statuettes and other ornaments of wood," but the figure is not primarily wood. The sisal is the largest single component at 40%, which points toward a vegetable-material classification, but the Styrofoam form and plastic twigs complicate this.

I'll go with the "other" basket-type heading:

{"hts_code": "4602.19.2900", "reason": "The Styrofoam form is covered mainly with natural vegetable materials (sisal, cones, leaves, wood chips), so it is classified as an other article of vegetable plaiting materials, though this is a low-confidence call."}
